name: vol_of_vol_signal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the 2-minute ATR is itself a time series whose own volatility (vol-of-vol) signals whether the index is in a stable-drift or regime-transition state. When vol-of-vol z-score is low (ATR has been nearly constant over 10 minutes), NIFTY is absorbing orders symmetrically around VWAP and RSI extremes on 2-minute bars reliably revert within 30-60 seconds as resting limit orders absorb directional flow. When vol-of-vol z-score rises above 0.5 (ATR itself becomes erratic), a large institutional TWAP order or macro trigger has disrupted the equilibrium — the EMA(1min)/EMA(3min) crossover during this regime confirms a directional order flow shift that persists for 60-90 seconds before the next equilibrium forms.

indicators.name: atr_24
indicators.formula: ATR(high, low, close, 24) with Wilder smoothing
indicators.purpose: 24 bars = 2-minute true range volatility. Original used ATR(14) on 1-min = 14-minute context; we compress to 2 minutes because for a 30-90s hold we care about CURRENT micro-volatility, not a 14-minute structural view. 24 bars is long enough to be non-noisy but short enough to detect rapid ATR changes.

indicators.name: vov_30
indicators.purpose: 30 bars = 2.5-minute rolling std of ATR. Same bar count as original (rolling_std over 30 bars) because the same number of ATR samples is needed to detect ATR instability — the key question is 'how many data points to measure std of ATR', not 'how many minutes'. 30 is the minimum for a statistically meaningful std estimate.

indicators.name: vov_z
indicators.purpose: Z-score baseline over 120 bars = 10 minutes. Original used 120-minute baseline; we use 10 minutes because NIFTY intraday regimes shift every 15-30 minutes (driven by session dynamics, not multi-hour cycles). A 10-minute baseline captures the current session's vol-of-vol norm without incorporating pre-lunch or pre-close regime differences.

indicators.name: rsi_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute RSI for mean-reversion signals in the stable regime. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min = 14-min context. Compressed to 2 minutes because stable-regime NIFTY RSI extremes at 5s bars require faster detection — the reversion window is 30-60 seconds, so we must identify the extreme quickly, not 14 minutes after it started.

indicators.name: ema_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute fast EMA for crossover breakout signals in the transitioning regime. At 5s bars, 12-bar EMA = 1-minute trend; faster than the 36-bar slow EMA by a 3:1 ratio, same ratio as original EMA(8)/EMA(21) ≈ 2.6:1.

indicators.name: ema_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute slow EMA for crossover context. Anchors the trend filter to a 3-minute view — short enough to be reactive to the regime transition (which is a new 1-2 minute directional move) but longer than ema_12 to give a clean crossover signal.

conditions: STABLE REGIME (vov_z < 0.5): RSI(24) < 32 — 2-minute selling exhaustion, expect mean reversion bounce
TRANSITIONING REGIME (0.5 <= vov_z < 2.0): EMA(12) crosses above EMA(36) — institutional flow shift confirmed by vol instability
buy_ce.confirmation: Both regime condition and directional signal must hold simultaneously on the same 5s bar

conditions: STABLE REGIME (vov_z < 0.5): RSI(24) > 68 — 2-minute buying exhaustion, expect mean reversion fade
TRANSITIONING REGIME (0.5 <= vov_z < 2.0): EMA(12) crosses below EMA(36) — downside institutional flow shift
buy_pe.confirmation: Both regime condition and directional signal must hold simultaneously on the same 5s bar

entry.no_trade_regime: vov_z >= 2.0 (volatile regime) — too chaotic for either mean reversion or directional breakout

exit.stop_rationale: Regime-adaptive: stable regime uses 3 pts (NIFTY mean reversion from RSI<32 should not retrace more than 6 spot pts before bouncing; 3 option pts at delta 0.5 = 6 spot pts threshold), transitioning regime uses 4 pts (breakout that reverses within 8 spot pts is a false regime classification). JSON scalar shows the transitioning value as the primary use case.
exit.target_rationale: Regime-adaptive: stable regime targets 5 pts (capturing ~50% of a typical 10-12 spot pt RSI-extreme reversion at 2-min horizon), transitioning regime targets 7 pts (15-25 spot pt breakout moves at 1-3 min horizon; 7 option pts = ~14 spot pts at delta 0.5, capturing ~60% of median move). JSON scalar shows average.

filters.vix_filter: none — vol-of-vol is itself the regime filter, making VIX redundant
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:25 IST; need 174 bars (14.5 min) of warmup for vov_z to stabilize
filters.volume_filter: none explicit — index volume is noisy at 5s; regime classification handles it implicitly
filters.trend_filter: built-in via regime: stable regime precludes trending breakout entries; transitioning regime precludes mean-reversion entries
filters.spread_filter: limit order execution — no spread cost; breakeven ~0.6 pts at scale

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — vol-of-vol regime classification depends on ATR stability which can produce false signals during news-driven spikes; regime boundaries (vov_z thresholds) need periodic recalibration

adaptation_notes: Converted from 1-min equity (NIFTY50 constituents) to 5-second NIFTY index options. Three key changes: (1) Lookbacks compressed from 14-min ATR / 30-min vol-of-vol / 120-min z-score to 2-min / 2.5-min / 10-min respectively — justified by hold time compression from 10-45 min to 30-90 sec; (2) Universe changed from individual stocks to NIFTY index — the vol-of-vol concept is MORE reliable on NIFTY because index ATR is smoother and less subject to single-stock event noise; (3) Regime-adaptive stops/targets replace the original ATR-percentage exits — option premium point calibration uses NIFTY typical move sizes at the relevant hold times.
weaknesses: ATR(24) on 5s bars is noisy — a single large-move bar can distort the vol-of-vol signal for the next 2 minutes
Regime boundary at vov_z=0.5/2.0 is sensitive; different market conditions may require different thresholds
EMA crossover in transitioning regime can be late — by the time ema_12 crosses ema_36, the initial move is partially captured
Running two distinct sub-strategies (mean reversion + breakout) means different days favor different sub-strategies, making net Sharpe moderate even if each sub-strategy is individually sound
